qt: to the Commission Nikolas Farantouris (S&D) Subject:

According to Eurostat, in 2025 6.3 % of the EU population, i.e. around 26.9 million people, faced severe material and social deprivation, a rate slightly lower than the 6.4 % in 20241. The highest rates were recorded in Romania (16.8 %), Bulgaria (15.0 %) and Greece (14.9 %), i.e. more than double the European average. The problem has a strong geographical dimension. Thirteen EU regions had rates between 16.8 % and 27.2 %, and three of these are in Greece: Central Macedonia, the Ionian Islands and the Peloponnese. Greece also has the second largest inter-regional gap, after Romania. This picture calls into question the objective of the European Pillar of Social Rights for 2030. It takes on particular importance in view of the negotiations on the multiannual financial framework (MFF) 2028-2034, where the future architecture of cohesion policy and social resources will determine support for the most vulnerable regions. In view of the above: 1.
How does the Commission assess the Eurostat data for Greece and the three most deprived Greek regions?
How will the Commission ensure that the new MFF will maintain sufficient and targeted resources for highly deprived regions such as Central Macedonia, the Ionian Islands and the Peloponnese?
Will the Commission include indicators of material and social deprivation in the criteria for allocating and monitoring MFF funds?
